original_value: Many Smart City projects are beginning to consider the role of citizens. However, current methods for engaging urban populations in participatory design (PD) activities are somewhat limited. In this article, we describe an approach taken to empower socially disadvantaged citizens, using a variety of both social and technological tools, in a Smart City project. Through analysing the nature of citizens’ concerns and proposed solutions, we explore the benefits of our approach, arguing that engaging citizens can uncover hyper-local concerns that provide a foundation for finding solutions to address citizen concerns. By reflecting on our approach, we identify four key challenges to utilising PD at an urban scale; balancing scale with the personal, who has control of the process, who is participating and integrating citizen-led work with local authorities. By addressing these challenges, we will be able to truly engage citizens as collaborators in co-designing their city.

result.paraphrase: Many Smart City initiatives are starting to account for the role of citizens. Yet existing ways of involving urban populations in participatory design (PD) activities remain somewhat restricted. In this article, we present an approach used in a Smart City project to empower socially disadvantaged citizens through a range of social and technological tools. By examining the nature of citizens’ concerns and the solutions they proposed, we consider the value of our approach, contending that citizen engagement can reveal hyper-local issues that form a basis for developing responses to those concerns. Reflecting on our approach, we identify four major challenges to using PD at urban scale: balancing scale with the personal, deciding who controls the process, determining who participates, and integrating citizen-led work with local authorities. Addressing these challenges will allow us to genuinely engage citizens as collaborators in co-designing their city.
